predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: 'the empire was divided between his two infant sons' on the death of Theodosius I; the western half, Honorius's share

successors.name: Kingdom of Odoacer
successors.text: Italy and the Danubian remnant, taken when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus on 4 September 476

successors.name: Kingdom of Soissons
successors.text: northern Gaul, where Syagrius held Aegidius's seat at Soissons

successors.name: Visigothic Kingdom
successors.text: Provence: Arles and Marseille 'occupied under Euric', undated; 'By 476, he had extended his rule to the Rhone and the Loire'

ledger.x: 395: the empire is divided and the Western Roman Empire begins at Milan.
401: the court leaves Milan for Ravenna.
402: Alaric's Visigoths enter Italy.
401-402: the northern frontier of Britain is given up.
403: the court returns to Rome.
31 December 406: the barbarian tribes cross the Rhine.
407: Britain follows the usurper.
407: Italy is clear of the Visigoths again.
408: the court returns to Ravenna.
early 408: Constans takes Hispania for his father.
May 408: Constantine III holds Gaul from Arles.
autumn 409: the invaders leave Gaul for Spain.
411: Constantius takes Gaul back from Gerontius's army.
411: north-eastern Spain is Honorius's again in Cliopatria's 410 shape.
August-September 411: Arles returns to Honorius.
413: the Visigoths take Narbonne and Toulouse.
413: the Burgundians settle on the Rhine as federates.
414: more of Tarraconensis is back.
417: Septimania is Roman again.
418: Honorius settles the Visigoths in Aquitaine as a vassal federation.
429: the Moors of Mauretania Caesariensis become militarily independent.
433: Aetius cedes part of Pannonia to the Huns.
435: the treaty gives the Vandals Numidia and Mauretania.
about 436: Aetius ends the Burgundian federation on the Rhine.
about 436: Aetius destroys the Burgundian federates.
437: the West recognises Eastern sovereignty over Illyricum.
439: the Salian Franks' land leaves the shape.
19 October 439: Carthage falls.
441: Sicily is lost to the Vandals.
442: the treaty closes the African war.
443: the Burgundians are resettled in Sapaudia.
445-450: Tournai and Cambrai go to the Franks.
450: the court moves to Rome.
7 April 451: Attila takes Metz and invades Gaul.
circa 20 June 451: the Huns turn back after the Catalaunian Plains.
452: Attila invades Italy.
452: Attila withdraws.
after 454: the Ostrogoths take Illyricum.
455: the Visigoths hold Aquitaine to the Garonne and beyond.
456-457: the Burgundians settle in Gaul.
457: the court returns to Ravenna.
456-458: the Visigoths hold Spain.
458: Sardinia goes to the Vandals.
459: Majorian recovers Spain.
late 458-459: Majorian restores Gaul.
457-461: Sicily returns under Marcellinus.
461: the court returns to Rome after Majorian's murder.
461-462: Sicily is lost again.
462: the Burgundians take Lyon and the Rhone valley.
462: Septimania leaves the shape.
462: the Rhine region goes to the Alamanni.
462: the Franks hold Belgica Secunda.
469: Euric takes Mérida and most of Lusitania.
469: the Suebi under Remismund take Lisbon.
471: Euric defeats the Romans at Arles and takes the city.
472: Euric takes Tarraconensis.
472: Euric conquers most of Hispania.
475: the Visigoths cease to be Roman federates.
475: Nepos cedes the lands south of the Loire to Euric.
475: Euric returns Provence in the treaty with Nepos.
28 August 475: Orestes takes Ravenna and Nepos flees.
476: northern Gaul is left to Syagrius at Soissons.
476: Provence goes to Euric.
476: the Western court is at Salona.
4 September 476: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus and rules Italy.
9 May 480: Julius Nepos is murdered and the Western Roman Empire ends.

wars.name: Alaric's invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: The court moved to Ravenna; no land was ceded in the pages read.

wars.name: Crossing of the Rhine
wars.outcome: The tribes ravaged Gaul and 'in autumn 409 much of the barbarian force entered Hispania'; the Rhine line was not restored until Constantius and the Burgundian settlement (413).

wars.name: Revolt of Constantine III
wars.outcome: Constantine took Britain (407), Gaul and, through his son Constans, Hispania (408), was recognised as co-emperor by Honorius in early 409, lost Hispania to Gerontius and Maximus in 409, was reduced to Arles by Gerontius in 411, and was beheaded in August or…

wars.name: Visigothic settlement in southern Gaul
wars.outcome: The Visigoths took Narbonne and Toulouse (413) and were settled in southwestern Gaul under Wallia in 418, 'as a vassal federation' with Toulouse as capital; the status lasted to 475.

wars.name: Wars of Theodoric I at Arles, Narbonne and Toulouse
wars.outcome: Theodoric I attacked Arles, was beaten at Narbonne in 436 and, defeated the allied Romans and Huns at Toulouse in 439; no border moved after the 418 settlement.

wars.name: Vandal conquest of Africa
wars.outcome: The Vandals crossed in 429, besieged Hippo in 430, were settled in Numidia and Mauretania by the treaty of 435, took Carthage in 439 and gained Byzacena, Tripolitania and part of Numidia by the treaty of 442.

wars.name: Aetius against the Burgundians
wars.outcome: Gundahar and many of the Burgundians were killed by Aetius, with Hun help, about 436; the survivors were resettled in Sapaudia in 443.

wars.name: Frankish advance on Tournai and Cambrai
wars.outcome: The Franks took Tournai and Cambrai 'probably in the period 445-450'.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of Gaul
wars.outcome: Attila crossed the Rhine in 451, took Metz on 7 April and reached Orléans; the Romans under Aetius, with the Visigoths under Theodoric, fought him at the Catalaunian Plains circa 20 June and he withdrew.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Attila ravaged north-eastern Italy, razed Aquileia after a three-month siege, halted at the Po and withdrew; he died early in 453.

wars.name: Vandal sack of Rome
wars.outcome: Gaiseric entered Rome; 'on 2 June 455, Pope Leo the Great received Gaiseric and implored him to abstain from murder'.

wars.name: Majorian's reconquest of Gaul and Hispania
wars.outcome: Majorian entered Gaul in late 458, forced the Visigoths to federate status and give up Hispania, campaigned against the Suebi through 459 and gathered a fleet in 460 that the Vandals destroyed; he was murdered on 7 August 461 and the gains were not held.

wars.name: Aegidius's refusal of Libius Severus
wars.outcome: Aegidius 'refused to recognize the new emperor Libius Severus (reigned 461-465), even threatening to invade Italy'; he held northern Gaul until his death in autumn 465, and his son Syagrius after him.

wars.name: Euric's conquests
wars.outcome: Euric took Mérida and most of Lusitania in 469, Arles after the Battle of Arles in 471, Tarraconensis (Visigothic page) and most of Hispania (Euric page) in 472, received the lands south of the Loire and west of the Rhone by the treaty of 475, which returned…

wars.name: Odoacer's revolt against Orestes
wars.outcome: The foederati proclaimed Odoacer king on 23 August 476, Orestes was killed at Placentia, Romulus Augustulus abdicated on 4 September and Odoacer ruled Italy; Nepos kept Dalmatia until his murder in 480.

certainty.note: No survey lines; frontiers are provinces or river lines.
